### Step 7 — Document

ADRs attach to decision **significance**, not to rigor: momentous (cross-wave, sets a precedent, expensive to reverse) gets one at any rigor; medium gets one when it will shape later waves; trivial gets none. `incident-response` writes the RCA instead. Where a doc made here lives is settled by one question — **who reads it unbidden?** Nobody → operational: park it at a path and cite the path when needed; nothing loads it, so its size costs nothing. Every session → knowledge: it reaches a reader only if the always-loaded index points at it, and that index is read in full, so it must earn its line or not be written.

**Promotion, before the release.** A durable record (each ADR the run wrote or amended, its design, its requirements) is copied into the project's tracked home, `docs-tracked:` in `.bionic/config.yaml`, `docs/` when absent: `session-poker.sh promote <adr|design|requirement> <path>`, one call per record, landing at `<home>/<kind>s/<name>`, the run number dropped. A plan, a log, a handoff and every other run record are operational: they stay under `.bionic/` and the verb refuses them.

**The release, last.** After review the release row lands on release-check.test.sh alone; the user approves that head, then it merges. Its entry pastes `session-poker.sh release-note`'s landing numbers whole, and `session-poker.sh known-limits-part <row>` commits its Known limits from the plan's deferrals.
